rationale:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-10, item 2 of COMMISSION_2026-08-10_owner_rulings_five_pieces.md — verbatim: "2. yes." The three readers of a deploy_image_asset result take a value they need and, when it is absent, do nothing at all: no log, no error, no work item. That is why a page shipping with no hero and no logo looked identical to a page that never wanted one, for five weeks (bugs_open/236). This is OBSERVABILITY ONLY: it does not widen what the readers accept, because doing so is bugs_open/236 §4 candidate 2 and is item 1's design decision, which the owner has explicitly reserved.

ONE DEPARTURE FROM THE COMMISSION'S LETTER, AND IT IS THE REVIEW QUESTION. The commission asked for a zap Warn. A Warn alone cannot be the evidence this exists to produce, because both places it would live are short-lived: (a) the pod log — these readers run in agent-chassis, whose own startup 'build provenance' line was measured absent from --tail=3000 hours after a roll on 2026-08-11; (b) the orchestration row — hero_deployed/logo_deployed exist only while the state is AWAITING_RESPONSES, because they ARE the awaited responses, and the live database-cleanup row prunes that status after FOUR hours (the repo seed at 020_scheduled_tasks.sql:739 says 24h and disagrees with the live row). The three observations of this bug (0 of 1,667 on 08-06 → 2 each on 08-09 → 0 again on 08-11) are one 4-hour window opening and closing. So the finding also goes to agent_error_log, which this codebase documents as the one sink that outlives an awaited step. Reviewers should judge whether that is a justified widening of 'add a Warn' or scope creep; the lane's position is that it is the same observability put where it survives, and that a Warn-only version would reproduce the evaporating-evidence problem it is meant to end.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE LOG LINE: commission item 5 shipped and its 090 re-run proved the diagnosis loop now works and the data is gone. So item 2 is now item 1's unblocker — it writes the evidence at the moment of failure instead of hunting for a row inside a 4-hour window.

plan.summary: Add one package-local helper, deployedImageURL, and route all three deploy_image_asset result readers through it. On a container that is PRESENT but carries no usable image_url it emits a zap.Warn and records one agent_error_log row (error_code DEPLOYED_IMAGE_RESULT_MISSING_URL, severity warning) naming the key it wanted and the keys the container actually held. On an ABSENT container it does nothing at all — most pages deploy no hero or logo, so the container key's presence is the demand gate, and that no-op is the property most likely to be got wrong. The row carries keys, never values. It also records fallback_sibling_present, which discriminates 'the container lost the key' from 'the URL is lost everywhere' — the question bugs_open/236 §5 leaves open.

edits.rationale: One helper rather than three else-branches, so the demand gate exists once and no call site can get it wrong. Unexported and package-local. Delegates the write to LogActionError, the existing actions-package door onto the single agent_error_log writer, which declares provenance inheritance on the caller's behalf (the running step genuinely is the right provenance for a reader's own finding).

Returns a container's keys, sorted, and nil for a non-map. KEYS, NEVER VALUES: the values behind these keys are base64 image payloads and full adapter response bodies, and the commission asked for 'its keys — not the whole value, which can be large'. Sorted so two rows of the same shape compare equal by eye and by string. A test asserts no value from the fixture reaches the payload.

The hero and logo readers (formerly the ok-guarded map accesses with no else at the lines the commission cited as :1020/:1031, actually :1125/:1136 by the time this lane opened) now go through the helper. Behaviour on the success path is unchanged — same key, same ContentData assignment, same Info log.

The third reader is the LAST rung of a three-rung ladder (render_context.logo_url → site_record.logo_url → logo_deployed.image_url), so reaching it means the two cheaper sources already failed and a miss there is a real 'this page gets no logo'. The audit call sits only on that rung, so a page whose logo came from an earlier rung files nothing. Takes ctx (as does its one caller, buildRenderContextFromParams); both are unexported and package-local, and the caller already had ctx in scope.

The no-op case, tested rather than assumed — BuildRenderContextAction runs for every page build and most pages deploy no hero or logo, so a regression here files a row per page fleet-wide. PROVEN BY MUTATION, not by the mock's own bookkeeping: replacing the presence guard with `if false && !present` makes this test fail on both of its assertions (the Warn count and the write-attempt detector). Restored and re-verified byte-identical afterwards.

Pins the durable row against the container shape measured on the live decisive row (bugs_open/236 §1): asserts error_code, severity, the sorted keys_present list that IS the 236 signature, and fallback_sibling_present. Nine further tests cover the healthy path, the keys-never-values property, the fallback discriminator, a non-map container, a lost row escalating to an Error log, the third reader's ladder short-circuit, and both first readers end to end through the real BuildRenderContextAction.

PROCESS_architecture_review.md as worded (owner ruling 2026-08-10 item 4): the trigger is "it adds, changes or removes an exported symbol other packages depend on". Every symbol here is unexported and package-local, so this is routed to the council gate rather than architecture review.
plan.risks:
1. THE DEPARTURE FROM 'A WARN' IS THE THING TO REVIEW. The commission asked for a log line; this adds a durable agent_error_log row as well. The justification is measured (4-hour prune on the exact status these keys live in; the pod log demonstrably not retaining startup lines on this service) and the mechanism is the documented one, but a reviewer may hold that widening a commissioned change is the submitter's to ask, not to decide. It is disclosed here rather than left to be discovered.

2. ROW VOLUME IS GATED ON DEMAND, NOT ON RATE, AND THE RATE IS UNMEASURED. Rows are filed only when a container key is present and unusable. [UNMEASURED] how often that is: bugs_open/236 §3 says explicitly that '2' was the count of rows in a retention window when someone looked, not an incidence rate, and warns against quoting it as one. If every image deploy hits this shape, the volume equals the fleet's hero+logo deploy rate. There is no rate limit and no dedupe. The lane's position is that one row per genuinely-broken deploy is the point, and that a page silently shipping without its hero is worth a row every time; but if the shape is universal this will be a steady producer until item 1 lands.

3. STATED BLIND SPOT: the demand gate is the container key's PRESENCE, so this is silent if some mechanism removes that key ENTIRELY. The observed shape has it present (coordinator.go:2719-2748 preserves-then-adds), so key-present is the shape to catch today, but whether the key-absent variant occurs is [UNMEASURED] and a reader cannot know locally that a deploy step was declared.

4. THE ROW'S CLAIM IS DELIBERATELY NARROW, AND COULD BE MISREAD. It asserts only that the CONTAINER carried no usable URL — not that the page shipped without an image, because the caller's own fallback (the deploy action's sibling collected_data key) may still supply one. fallback_sibling_present records which case it was, and the message is worded about the container. A reader who greps the error_code and assumes 'page has no hero' will overcount; the remedy string in the context says so.

5. SIGNATURE CHANGES: extractLogoURLFromParams and buildRenderContextFromParams gain a ctx parameter, and the latter's local RenderContext variable (previously named ctx) is renamed renderCtx. Both are unexported, package-local, and have one caller each, which already had ctx in scope. No exported symbol changes.

6. THE CODE IS ALREADY AT HEAD, AND NOT BY THIS LANE'S COMMIT. Another session's commit 038211dd8 swept these four files out of the shared working tree while this lane was mid-verification — the hazard CLAUDE.md documents ('it cannot stop a session that still runs git add -A from sweeping up yours, half-finished'). Checked and reported rather than assumed: HEAD carries the RESTORED, unmutated code (the mutation proof had already been reverted), a clean `git archive HEAD` checkout builds and the actions suite passes there, and all four files at HEAD are byte-identical to the reviewed working tree. This submission therefore reviews code that is already committed and will ride the next fleet roll; per the 2026-07-29 owner ruling, review here is after the fact by design and no ordering constraint is claimed.
